# Submitting a Simple R Job with Slurm on Atlas

This tutorial demonstrates a two-stage Slurm workflow:

1. Submit `simdat.R` to generate a CSV file.
2. Inspect the generated data in an interactive R session.
3. Edit the existing batch script with `nano` so that it runs `run_model.R`.
4. Submit the revised batch script to fit a linear model.
5. Load and inspect the saved model in an interactive R session.

The example uses the `disease_ecology` project allocation and the Atlas `r/4.5` module. Replace the project name or module version where required for another allocation or system.

## Example files

The workflow uses three files:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`simdat.R`](examples/simdat.R) | Generates 1,000 simulated observations and writes `data_2026-08-03.csv`. |
| [`run_model.R`](examples/run_model.R) | Reads the CSV file, fits `lm(y ~ x)`, and saves the fitted model as `model_output.RData`. |
| [`simdat.sh`](examples/simdat.sh) | Requests Slurm resources, loads modules, and initially runs `simdat.R`. |

The example files are also available in the [`2026-04-16-SciNet_HPC_overview`](https://github.com/geoepi/sandbox/tree/main/2026-04-16-SciNet_HPC_overview) directory on GitHub.

## 1. Log in to Atlas Open OnDemand

Log in to the Atlas Open OnDemand interface. From the top navigation bar, select **Files**, then select **/project**.

![Open the project filesystem from the Files menu](2026-08-03-submit_slurm/figures/fig_1.png)

## 2. Navigate to the project directory

In the file browser, select **Change directory**. Enter:

```text
/project/disease_ecology
```

Select **OK**.

![Change the file browser to the disease_ecology project directory](2026-08-03-submit_slurm/figures/fig_2.png)

## 3. Create a working directory

Select **New Directory** and enter a directory name. The notes use `mytest-john`; use any unique and informative name.

![Create a new working directory](2026-08-03-submit_slurm/figures/fig_3.png)

Open the new directory after it is created.

## 4. Upload the example files

Select **Upload** in the upper-right corner of the file browser. Drag the following files into the upload window:

- `simdat.R`
- `run_model.R`
- `simdat.sh`

Select **Upload** to finish.

![Upload the three example files](2026-08-03-submit_slurm/figures/fig_4.png)

The working directory should now contain all three files.

## 5. Open a terminal

Select **Open in Terminal** from the file browser toolbar. The terminal should open in the current working directory.

![Open a terminal in the current directory](2026-08-03-submit_slurm/figures/fig_5.png)

Confirm the location and files:

```bash
pwd
ls -lh
```

The output should show the working directory and the three uploaded files.

## 6. Start an interactive development session

Run the development-session command shown in the notes:

```bash
srun --account=disease_ecology \
  --partition=development \
  --nodes=1 \
  --ntasks=16 \
  --pty bash
```

Wait until Slurm allocates the resources. The hostname in the prompt should change from an Atlas login node to an Atlas development node, for example:

```text
[john.humphreys@atlas-devel-1 mytest-john]$
```

Confirm that the current directory still contains the example files:

```bash
pwd
ls -lh
```

## 7. Submit the data-generation job

Submit the batch script:

```bash
sbatch simdat.sh
```

A successful submission returns a numeric job identifier:

```text
Submitted batch job 20457490
```

Record the job identifier. The examples below use a shell variable so the output file can be referenced consistently:

```bash
JOBID=20457490
```

Replace `20457490` with the identifier returned for the actual job.

### Correct Windows line endings when necessary

Files uploaded from Windows may contain DOS/Windows line endings. In that case, `sbatch` reports:

```text
sbatch: error: Batch script contains DOS line breaks (\r\n)
sbatch: error: instead of expected UNIX line breaks (\n).
```

Convert the batch script to Unix line endings and resubmit it:

```bash
dos2unix simdat.sh
sbatch simdat.sh
```

Update `JOBID` with the identifier from the successful submission.

## 8. Monitor the job

List the user's active jobs:

```bash
squeue -u "$USER"
```

Common state codes include:

- `PD`: pending
- `R`: running

The job will disappear from `squeue` after it finishes. The example scripts include a 30-second delay, so the jobs should remain visible briefly.

## 9. Check the data-generation results

List the directory contents after the job finishes:

```bash
ls -lh
```

The directory should now contain:

```text
data_2026-08-03.csv
run_model.R
simdat.R
simdat.sh
slurm-20457490.out
```

The Slurm output filename uses the job identifier. Inspect it with:

```bash
cat "slurm-${JOBID}.out"
```

The final message should be:

```text
[1] "Data generation complete!"
```

Verify that the CSV file is present and nonempty:

```bash
ls -lh data_2026-08-03.csv
head data_2026-08-03.csv
```

## 10. Inspect the generated data in an interactive R session

Load R and start an interactive session:

```bash
module load r/4.5
R
```

At the R prompt, read and inspect the data:

```r
mydata <- read.csv("data_2026-08-03.csv")

dim(mydata)
head(mydata)
summary(mydata)
```

`dim(mydata)` should return 1,000 rows and 2 columns:

```text
[1] 1000    2
```

The first six rows should begin as follows because `simdat.R` uses `set.seed(123)`:

```text
            x           y
1 -0.56047565 -0.99579872
2 -0.23017749 -1.03995504
3  1.55870831 -0.01798024
4  0.07050839 -0.13217513
5  0.12928774 -2.54934277
6  1.71506499  1.04057346
```

Exit R without saving a workspace image:

```r
q()
```

Enter `n` when R asks:

```text
Save workspace image? [y/n/c]: n
```

## 11. Edit the batch script with `nano`

The data file now exists. Modify `simdat.sh` so that the next Slurm job runs `run_model.R` instead of `simdat.R`.

Open the script:

```bash
nano simdat.sh
```

Make two edits.

First, change the job name from:

```bash
#SBATCH --job-name=simdat
```

to:

```bash
#SBATCH --job-name=run_model
```

Second, change the final command from:

```bash
Rscript --no-save --no-restore simdat.R
```

to:

```bash
Rscript --no-save --no-restore run_model.R
```

Save and close the file:

1. Press `Ctrl+O` to write the file.
2. Press `Enter` to confirm the filename.
3. Press `Ctrl+X` to exit `nano`.

Confirm the edited lines:

```bash
grep -nE 'job-name|Rscript' simdat.sh
```

The result should resemble:

```text
2:#SBATCH --job-name=run_model
23:Rscript --no-save --no-restore run_model.R
```

Line numbers may differ if the script was otherwise edited.

## 12. Submit the model job

Submit the revised batch script:

```bash
sbatch simdat.sh
```

Record the new job identifier:

```text
Submitted batch job 20457500
```

Store it separately from the data-generation job identifier:

```bash
MODEL_JOBID=20457500
```

Replace `20457500` with the actual identifier.

Monitor the job:

```bash
squeue -u "$USER"
```

Do not proceed until the model job has finished.

## 13. Check the model-job results

List the directory contents:

```bash
ls -lh
```

The directory should now include:

```text
model_output.RData
slurm-20457500.out
```

Inspect the batch output:

```bash
cat "slurm-${MODEL_JOBID}.out"
```

The output should contain both:

```text
[1] "Linear model analysis complete!"
```

and the printed result from:

```r
summary(model)
```

The model summary should include the model call, residual summary, coefficient table, residual standard error, R-squared values, and F-statistic.

Verify that the saved model file exists and is nonempty:

```bash
ls -lh model_output.RData
```

## 14. Inspect the linear-model results interactively

Start R again if it is no longer running:

```bash
module load r/4.5
R
```

Load the saved workspace object and inspect the fitted model:

```r
load("model_output.RData")

ls()
class(model)
summary(model)
coef(model)
```

Expected structural checks are:

```text
[1] "model"
[1] "lm"
```

`summary(model)` should reproduce the linear-model results printed in the second Slurm output file. `coef(model)` should return an intercept and a coefficient for `x`.

Exit R without saving another workspace image:

```r
q()
```

Enter `n` when prompted.

## 15. Completion check

The tutorial is complete when the working directory contains all of the following:

```text
simdat.R
run_model.R
simdat.sh
data_2026-08-03.csv
model_output.RData
slurm-<data-job-id>.out
slurm-<model-job-id>.out
```

Both Slurm output files should show successful completion, and the CSV data and fitted `lm` object should have been inspected in interactive R sessions.

## Troubleshooting

### `Batch script contains DOS line breaks`

Run:

```bash
dos2unix simdat.sh
```

Then resubmit the script.

### `cannot open file 'data_2026-08-03.csv'`

The model job cannot find the data file. Confirm that:

```bash
pwd
ls -lh data_2026-08-03.csv
```

The model job must be submitted from the same directory containing the CSV file, unless the scripts are changed to use explicit paths.

### The job no longer appears in `squeue`

A completed job is removed from the active queue. Check the corresponding Slurm output file:

```bash
ls -lt slurm-*.out
cat "slurm-${JOBID}.out"
```

### No `model_output.RData` file was created

Inspect the model job's output file for an R error:

```bash
cat "slurm-${MODEL_JOBID}.out"
```

Also confirm that `simdat.sh` runs `run_model.R`:

```bash
grep -n 'Rscript' simdat.sh
```
